decision: Use the CUDA-Graph row only as an external performance-headroom observation. Do not use either row as a correctness, determinism, quality, or milestone-acceptance baseline.

reported_quantization.validation_scope: Compression metadata for the configured Linear targets and declared ignore list; not an independent validation of every tensor payload.
reported_quantization.normalization: The harness validated the configured compression-metadata contract and passed an in-memory null-to-minus-one hf_overrides normalization. It did not alter checkpoint files.

development_comparison.warning: The engines use different checkpoints, weight formats, and prefill timing boundaries. These ratios compare reported metrics to identify optimization headroom only; they are not isolated engine-speed, model-quality, or numerical-parity comparisons.
development_comparison.vllm_prefill_timing_boundary: vLLM first_token_latency, including request and first-token selection work
development_comparison.gem16_prefill_timing_boundary: first prefill launch through prefill synchronization, excluding first-token head selection

limitations: The community W4A16 checkpoint is not the same weight artifact or quantization recipe as gem16's compiled mixed FP8/NVFP4 checkpoint or Google's official QAT Q4_0 GGUF. No quality equivalence has been established.

All three CUDA-Graph outputs and all three Eager outputs had different full-token hashes despite greedy temperature-zero sampling. The first output token was stable in all six runs, but no output-quality claim is made and this does not qualify correctness.

The common Eager divergence rules out CUDA Graph replay as the necessary cause. Marlin W4A16/MoE, Triton attention, FP8 KV, and other shared numerical or scheduling paths remain possible sources; no root cause was established.

The current harness records one complete representative token stream and only hashes plus first and last IDs for the other runs, so the first intra-mode divergence position and top-logit margins are not available.
The CUDA-Graph row uses gpu_memory_utilization=0.985 and external telemetry observed only 63 MiB free at peak. This is too little margin for a production memory policy.

Both successful modes emitted non-fatal CUDACachingAllocator OOM warnings for 1,476,395,008-byte and 127,926,272-byte allocations during initialization. Startup continued, positive Marlin dispatch lines remained present, and no fallback line was observed, but the warnings must accompany the result.
Gemma 4's heterogeneous head dimensions forced TRITON_ATTN because FA4 was unavailable in this environment.
The Graph-versus-Eager comparison is not an isolated CUDA-Graph A/B test: Eager also disables torch.compile, uses a lower memory-utilization setting, and the graph run used a warm compile cache.
The one-warm-up, three-measurement protocol is a bounded development characterization, not the formal M20 three-warm-up/ten-retained qualification protocol.

The Eager benchmark wrote its complete result after all measurements and the benchmark process exited successfully; the isolation service then reported a teardown timeout and returned wrapper status 1. Its log does not identify a remaining process after EngineCore reports exiting its busy loop.
The CUDA-Graph service also force-killed its lingering EngineCore after the result was complete, although the service itself returned success.

External 200 ms nvidia-smi telemetry spans startup, benchmark, and teardown rather than only retained measurement windows. It is device-wide rather than process-attributed, and no idle baseline is subtracted.
No pre-run record was made of the platform power profile, nvidia-powerd state, configured power limit, starting temperature, or absence of other GPU processes.
